concepts.title: Lorentz Force on a Moving Charge
concepts.definition: The total electromagnetic force experienced by a moving charged particle when passing through regions containing both electric and magnetic fields.
concepts.key_idea: Magnetic force acts perpendicular to both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both velocity and magnetic field vectors.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic force on a charge moving in a magnetic field
what is the lorentz force on an electron moving perpendicular to a magnetic field
find the force experienced by a proton entering a magnetic field
how much magnetic force acts on a charge moving parallel to the field

solution_steps.explain: Multiply charge, velocity, magnetic field, and the sine of the angle between velocity and field.

concepts.title: Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor
concepts.definition: The macroscopic magnetic force exerted on a straight wire carrying electric current inside an external magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, the total force is the total of magnetic forces acting on all individual drift charge carriers.
question_patterns: calculate the force on a current carrying wire in a magnetic field
find the magnetic force per unit length on a conductor
how much force acts on a straight wire carrying current perpendicular to a magnetic field
what is the force on a wire placed at an angle to the magnetic field

solution_steps.action: calculate magnetic force on the wire
solution_steps.explain: Multiply current, length of the wire, magnetic field strength, and the sine of the angle between the wire direction and the field.

concepts.title: Radius of Circular Path in a Magnetic Field
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the circular's radius orbit described by a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: The magnetic force provides the necessary centripetal force for circular motion.
question_patterns: find the radius of the circular path of an electron in a magnetic field
calculate the radius of orbit for a proton moving perpendicular to a magnetic field
what is the radius of the circle described by a charged particle
how does the radius of the path change with velocity

solution_steps.explain: Multiply mass and velocity of the particle.
Multiply charge and magnetic field.
Divide momentum by the denominator product.

concepts.title: Frequency of Circular Motion in a Magnetic Field
concepts.definition: The number of revolutions completed per unit time by a charged particle orbiting in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, the orbital frequency does not depend on the particle's both speed and orbit radius.
question_patterns: calculate the frequency of revolution of an electron in a magnetic field
find the cyclotron frequency of a proton
what is the frequency of rotation of a charged particle in a magnetic field
how much is the frequency of an orbiting charge

solution_steps.explain: Multiply charge and magnetic field.
Multiply 2, pi, and mass.
Divide the numerator by the denominator.

concepts.title: Biot-Savart Law
concepts.definition: A fundamental law that describes the infinitesimal magnetic field produced at a point in space by a tiny current-carrying element.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the magnetic field scales with current and element length, and in inverse proportion with the distance's square.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic field due to a small current element
find the magnetic field at a point using biot savart law
what is the magnetic field produced by a short wire segment

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the constant 1e-7, current, element length, and sine of the angle.
Square the distance from the element to the point.
Divide the numerator by the denominator.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field at the Centre of a Circular Loop
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the magnetic field formed at the geometric center of a circular coil carrying a steady electric current.
concepts.key_idea: The field is strongest at the center and is indeed directed along the loop's axis.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic field at the center of a circular coil
find the magnetic field at the center of a loop
what is the field at the center of a tightly wound coil
how much is the magnetic field at the center of a circular current loop

solution_steps.explain: Multiply 2 * pi * 1e-7 by the number of turns and current, then divide by the radius.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field on the Axis of a Circular Loop
concepts.definition: The magnetic field at a point along the central axis perpendicular to the plane of a circular current-carrying loop.
concepts.key_idea: The axial field decreases as the loop's distance from the center increases.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic field on the axis of a circular loop
find the axial magnetic field of a current carrying coil
what is the magnetic field at a distance along the axis of a circular loop

solution_steps.explain: Multiply 2 * pi * 1e-7 by current and the square of the radius.
Raise the sum of squared radius and squared distance to the power of 1.5.
Divide the numerator by the denominator.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field of an Infinite Straight Wire
concepts.definition: In brief, the magnetic field formed by an infinitely long, straight conductor carrying a steady electric current, derived using Ampere's law.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the magnetic field lines form concentric circles around the wire, and the field strength varies in inverse proportion with distance.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic field due to a long straight wire
find the magnetic field at a distance from an infinite wire
what is the field of a long current carrying conductor
how much is the magnetic field near a straight wire

solution_steps.explain: Multiply 2 * 1e-7 by current and divide by distance.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field of a Solenoid
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, the uniform magnetic field generated inside a tightly wound, long helical coil holding a steady current.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the magnetic field inside a long solenoid is nearly uniform and directed along its longitudinal axis, while the external field is negligible.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic field inside a solenoid
find the field near the center of a long solenoid
what is the magnetic field of a solenoid with given turns and current

solution_steps.explain: Divide total turns by the length of the solenoid.
Multiply mu_0 (4 * pi * 1e-7) by turns per unit length and current.

concepts.title: Force Between Parallel Currents
concepts.definition: The mutual magnetic force per unit length exerted between two long, straight, parallel conductors holding steady currents.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Parallel currents moving in the common direction attract each other, while antiparallel currents repel.
question_patterns: calculate the force per unit length between two parallel wires
find the force on a section of wire due to a parallel wire
what is the force between two long straight parallel current carrying conductors
how much mutual force is exerted between two parallel currents

solution_steps.explain: Multiply 2 * 1e-7 by current_a and current_b, then divide by distance.

solution_steps.action: calculate total force on a section
solution_steps.explain: Multiply force per unit length by the section length.

concepts.title: Torque on a Current Loop
concepts.definition: The rotational torque felt by a planar current-carrying loop suspended in a uniform outside magnetic field.
concepts.formula: torque = turns * current * area * field * sin_theta
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, a current loop behaves as a magnetic dipole with a magnetic moment vector perpendicular to its plane.
question_patterns: calculate the torque on a rectangular current loop
find the torque experienced by a coil in a magnetic field
what is the maximum torque on a current carrying loop
how much torque acts on a magnetic dipole in a field

solution_steps.explain: Multiply turns, current, and area of the loop.
Multiply magnetic moment, magnetic field, and sine of the angle.

concepts.title: Sensitivity of a Moving Coil Galvanometer
concepts.definition: The measure of a galvanometer's responsiveness, defined as the angular deflection produced per unit electric current or unit potential difference.
concepts.key_idea: Current sensitivity depends on the coil area, number of turns, magnetic field strength, and torsional spring constant.
question_patterns: calculate the current sensitivity of a galvanometer
find the ratio of current sensitivities of two meters
what is the voltage sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer

solution_steps.explain: Multiply turns, area, and field, then divide by the spring constant.
Divide current sensitivity by resistance.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A straight wire of mass {mass} g and length {length} m carries a current of {current} A. It is suspended in mid-air by a uniform horizontal magnetic field B. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field?

extracted_variables.mass: mass of the wire in grams
extracted_variables.length: length of the wire in meters

solution_template.explain: Divide mass in grams by 1000 to get mass in kilograms.
Multiply mass in kg by acceleration due to gravity (9.8 m/s^2).
Divide gravitational force by the product of current and length.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Consider a tightly wound {turns} turn coil of radius {radius} cm, carrying a current of {current} A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil?

extracted_variables.turns: number of turns in the coil
extracted_variables.radius: radius of the coil in centimeters

solution_template.explain: Divide radius in cm by 100 to get radius in meters.
Use the formula for magnetic field at the center of a circular coil.
